title: Annotatio III §.IV: Sagittarius — painters’ insane opinion; flesh-image apology = Nestorian diabolic invention
pass_a_gloss: That they said: What is this insane opinion of painters, that for the sake of base and wretched gain they strive to fashion what they cannot effect, and intend with impious hands to figure even those things confessed only by mouth and heart? But condemned by stout-hearted men in that they themselves strove to paint Christ’s incomprehensible and uncircumscribable Divine nature, they flee by a wicked invention to another apology — that they exhibit an image of the flesh alone, which we saw and handled and with which we lived: which is indeed impious and a Nestorian Diabolic invention.
pass_b_english: Sagittarius’s quote: what insane painters’ opinion — for base gain they try to figure with impious hands what mouth and heart alone confess?
Condemned for painting Christ’s incomprehensible, uncircumscribable Divine nature, they invent a flesh-only image apology — impious, and a Nestorian diabolic invention.
source_text: Quòd dixerint: Quænam est hæc insana opinio pictorum, ut lucri turpis & miseri causa ea quæ efficere nequeunt, studeant conficere, ut & ea quæ ore & corde sunt tantummodo confessa, impiis manibus figurare intendant? Damnati autem à cordatis viris in eo quòd incomprehensibilem & incircumscriptibilem Divinam Christi naturam ipsi depingere studuerunt, ad aliam aliquam pravâ inventione apologiam confugiunt, quòd solius carnis, quam vidimus & palpavimus & cum qua versati sumus, illius, inquam, imaginem exhibeant: quod sane impium est & Nestoriana Diabolica inventio.
